records.title: Digital Signal Processing
records.summary: Covers discrete-time signals, Fourier transforms, and the design of digital filters.
records.learning_note: Use the Fourier transform to diagnose spectral interference before designing a filter.
records.first_activity: Plot the frequency spectrum of two sampled tones before and after applying a low-pass filter.

records.title: Digital Communications Systems
records.summary: Studies digital modulation, receivers, and communication over channels with noise and intersymbol interference.
records.learning_note: Model how noise affects receiver decisions in a digital link.
records.first_activity: Simulate a simple digital link and plot the fraction of incorrect symbols as noise increases.

records.title: Automatic Control
records.summary: Introduces time- and frequency-domain models for linear feedback systems, stability, and controller design.
records.learning_note: Relate a robot's motor response to feedback, stability, and the choice of controller gain.
records.first_activity: Plot a simulated DC motor speed step response at two different controller gains.

records.title: Digital Control Systems
records.summary: Models and designs discrete controllers using sampled signals, z-transforms, stability analysis, and microprocessors.
records.learning_note: Connect sampled sensor readings and software timing to a digital controller's response.
records.first_activity: Compare the same simulated motor controller using two sampling intervals.

records.title: Computer Networking
records.summary: Examines computer networks and distributed systems, including routing, end-to-end protocols, and congestion control.
records.learning_note: Explore how packets move once a link can carry signals. This complements the physical-layer work in ECE communications.
records.first_activity: Draw how a packet crosses a wireless link and a router, then explain the job of each layer.

records.title: Geometric Algorithms
records.summary: Studies methods for computing with geometric objects, with applications including robotics, mapping, and sensor networks.
records.learning_note: Build the geometry skills used in planning and mapping. Feedback control then helps a robot follow a planned motion.
records.first_activity: Use a set of 2D points to represent obstacles and find the nearest point along a simulated route.

records.title: PySDR: Signals and frequency-domain practice
records.summary: An online guide to digital signal processing and software-defined radio in Python, with topics including sampling, Fourier transforms, and filtering.
records.first_activity: Generate a waveform in Python and compare its time and frequency plots. Use the simulation examples if you have no radio hardware.

records.title: DC Motor Speed: PID Controller Design
records.summary: A MATLAB tutorial that models DC motor speed and compares the step responses of proportional and PID controllers.
records.first_activity: Compare the tutorial's step-response plots and identify how much the speed overshoots and how long it takes to settle.

records.title: Signals & Communications
records.summary: Use signal and communications coursework to explore digital signal processing, radio frequency engineering, and wireless systems. Software-defined radio and open radio networks give students areas to explore.

records.title: Controls & Robotics
records.summary: Use modeling, feedback, and stability analysis to explore robotics, controls, and industrial automation. Mobile robots and manufacturing systems provide examples of these techniques in use.

records.title: Digital VLSI Systems Design
records.summary: Study the design, timing, analysis, and physical layout of digital CMOS circuits, from transistors and logic gates to sequential circuits and data paths.
records.learning_note: Connect digital logic to circuit-level tradeoffs in delay, noise margins, and layout.
records.first_activity: Compare two CMOS logic implementations and explain how gate capacitance can affect propagation delay.

records.title: Computer Architecture and Design
records.summary: Examines processor, memory, and interconnect organization, including pipelining, caches, multicore systems, and architectural design tradeoffs.
records.learning_note: Follow chip design into processor architecture and performance tradeoffs.
records.first_activity: Trace two instructions through a simple processor pipeline and identify a source of stalls.

records.title: Semiconductor Processing
records.summary: Surveys semiconductor fabrication steps, from wafer preparation through patterning, doping, etching, and metallization.
records.learning_note: Connect semiconductor device concepts to the steps and equipment used in a fabrication facility.
records.first_activity: Sketch a simple fabrication sequence and identify one purpose and one measurement for each step.

records.title: Quality Engineering
records.summary: Applies statistical process control, process capability analysis, and designed experiments to manufacturing and quality improvement.
records.learning_note: Use control charts and capability measures to investigate process variability and yield. The course page recommends SIE 305.
records.first_activity: Compare two simulated manufacturing lots using a control chart and explain which one warrants investigation.

records.title: Physical Properties of Materials
records.summary: Introduces solid-state explanations for materials' thermal, electrical, optical, and magnetic behavior.
records.learning_note: Build materials background for device physics. The course page lists MSE 222 or MSE 223R, concurrent OPTI 240, or department consent.
records.first_activity: Compare materials with different electrical and thermal properties and explain how the differences affect a device.

records.title: Verilator Create-Binary Example
records.summary: The Verilator project demonstrates compiling a small SystemVerilog design and running it as a standalone simulation.
records.first_activity: Use the example build flow to simulate a four-bit counter. Check reset, counting, and rollover.

records.title: Semiconductors & Digital Hardware
records.summary: Digital hardware designers and verification engineers build and test logic. Fabrication, process equipment, product testing, and advanced packaging are related areas with different learning routes.

records.title: Operating System Design
records.summary: Studies operating-system facilities and practical low-level C development, with system diagnostics and tools.
records.learning_note: Build systems knowledge for firmware and real-time work. Pair it with the separate FreeRTOS scheduling exercise.

records.title: Advanced Motion Control
records.summary: Uses modeling and control methods to study advanced motion-control systems.
records.learning_note: Connect feedback and digital control concepts to motion and actuator behavior.

records.title: Antenna Theory and Design
records.summary: Applies electromagnetic principles to antenna behavior and design.
records.learning_note: Connect electromagnetics with antenna performance in a communications system.

records.title: Microwave Engineering I: Passive Circuit Design
records.summary: Develops microwave analysis and design techniques for passive circuits and components.
records.learning_note: Explore matching and other passive-circuit concepts before studying active microwave designs.

records.title: Microwave Engineering II: Active Circuit Design
records.summary: Studies active microwave circuits and design methods for high-frequency electronics.
records.learning_note: Connect microwave circuit concepts to the active devices used in radio hardware.

records.title: Fundamentals of Optics for Electrical Engineers
records.summary: Covers geometrical and Fourier optics, diffraction, optical aberrations, beams, and electro-optic components.
records.learning_note: Use geometrical and wave-optics models to understand optical imaging systems.

records.title: Lasers and Photonics
records.summary: Introduces lasers, the behavior of laser light, and photonic devices used in displays, fibers, and optical communications.
records.learning_note: The catalog suggests MATH 223 and OPTI 341 as preparation. Check the requirements for your section.

records.title: Photonics Communications
records.summary: Applies optical component physics to fiber communications, including attenuation, dispersion, modulation, detection, and receiver performance.
records.learning_note: The catalog lists prior circuits and optical lab preparation, including OPTI 380A and 380B. Check section access.

records.title: Photovoltaic Solar Energy Systems
records.summary: Studies photovoltaic operation, solar illumination, and the design and evaluation of solar-energy systems.
records.learning_note: Study how electrical and device concepts apply to photovoltaic generation. Use the energy-storage resource to explore how generation and load interact.

records.title: Measurement and Data Analysis in Biomedical Engineering
records.summary: Covers biomedical measurement and instrumentation, from sensors and physiological signals to acquisition, analysis, and measurement safety.
records.learning_note: Connect circuits and signal processing to instrumentation. Use simulated signals for the practice activity.

records.title: Introduction to Computer Vision
records.summary: Studies computer vision algorithms for image formation, filtering, geometry, segmentation, tracking, and recognition.
records.learning_note: The catalog lists probability and computer graphics as helpful preparation. Check CS section access and ECE elective approval.

records.title: Principles of Machine Learning
records.summary: Introduces machine-learning methods for learning from data and evaluating predictions and decisions.
records.learning_note: The catalog recommends Calculus I and programming at the CSC 120 level. Check CS section access and ECE elective approval.

records.title: Practical Optics
records.summary: Introduces practical optical concepts and systems to students across engineering disciplines.
records.learning_note: The catalog lists PHYS 241. Check the section’s prerequisites and ECE elective approval.

records.title: Power system Engineering
records.summary: Introduces analysis and design of electrical power systems for residential and commercial buildings.
records.learning_note: The department lists ENGR 211M. Confirm section access and ECE elective approval.

records.title: Biomedical Instrumentation
records.summary: Combines theory and practice in biomedical measurements, including sensors, signal acquisition, noise reduction and experimental analysis.
records.learning_note: Explore the instrumentation side of biomedical sensing. Ask the BME department about section access and ECE advising about elective use.

records.title: Biomedical Imaging
records.summary: Introduces the engineering principles of biomedical imaging methods, including optical imaging, CT, and MRI.
records.learning_note: The course page lists College of Engineering Advanced Standing or department consent. Check section access and ECE elective approval.

records.title: FreeRTOS Tasks and Co-routines
records.summary: Introduces tasks and scheduling concepts in the FreeRTOS kernel.
records.first_activity: Draw a timeline for two periodic tasks and explain how a priority change affects the schedule.

records.title: LiteRT Post-Training Quantization
records.summary: The Google AI Edge documentation explains options for quantizing trained models for efficient inference.
records.first_activity: Compare the size, runtime and accuracy of the same small model before and after quantization.

records.title: Wyant College Photonics Research
records.summary: UArizona describes examples of photonics in imaging, optical networks, devices, and laser research.
records.first_activity: Choose one application and explain what the system does with light.

records.title: DOE Solar Energy and Storage Basics
records.summary: The Department of Energy explains why storage is paired with solar generation and compares common storage technologies.
records.first_activity: Use a fictional hourly solar and load profile to show when storage would charge or discharge.

records.title: NIBIB Introduction to MRI
records.summary: A National Institutes of Health overview of magnetic resonance imaging and the role of the equipment in producing images.
records.first_activity: Explain the difference between collecting a signal and reconstructing an image from it.

records.title: Photonics & Electro-Optics
records.summary: Optical and photonics work links imaging, optical devices, lasers, and fiber communications. The two study routes emphasize different system applications.

records.title: Power & Energy Systems
records.summary: Power and renewable-energy work can build on circuit theory, photovoltaic generation, storage and building electrical systems.

records.title: Biomedical Instrumentation & Sensors
records.summary: Biomedical instrumentation and imaging use electronics, sensors, signal processing, and testing to support medical technologies.

records.title: MIT OpenCourseWare · Transmission Lines and Reflection
records.summary: Lectures 10 and 11 cover transmission lines and reflection by loads.
records.first_activity: Plot the reflected power fraction for a matched load and two mismatched loads.

records.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook · Process Capability
records.summary: NIST explains how to compare process variation with specification limits.
records.first_activity: Plot measurements for two simulated wafer lots against a specification limit and report their pass rates.

records.title: OpenStax · Power in an AC Circuit
records.summary: This section covers average AC power, RMS voltage and current, and power factor.
records.first_activity: Make a table of real power, apparent power and power factor for two fictional building loads.

records.title: PhysioNet · MIT-BIH Noise Stress Test Database
records.summary: The database description identifies baseline wander, muscle artifact and electrode motion artifact.
records.first_activity: Add drift and high-frequency noise to a synthetic pulse, then plot the filtered signal and compare the error.
